newsitem.title: USA: Clinton minimizes impact of Yeltsin heart problems.
newsitem.headline: Clinton minimizes impact of Yeltsin heart problems.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Monday he was confident U.S. relations with nuclear-armed Russia would "proceed on a normal course" despite Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health problems.
Responding to a reporter's question during a White House bill-signing ceremony, Clinton said the Russian government had "come a long way in developing constitutional mechanisms of authority."
He said the United States maintained "regular contact" with other top Kremlin officials including Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.
"I feel comfortable right now that our relationship will proceed on a normal course," Clinton said.

Yeltsin has said he would have heart surgery at the end of this month. But doctors have not set a date for the surgery to improve the blood supply to the Russian leader's heart and top heart surgeon Renat Akchurin, who is expected to lead the operation, said this weekend that surgery might be delayed for six to eight weeks and there was a risk of the operation being cancelled altogether if Yeltsin's health did not permit it.
